surface_mechanism_description: The text discusses the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to grow NbN films for superconducting nanowires, which are used in quantum phase slip (CQPS) devices. The ALD process involves a self-limiting surface reaction principle with a well-controlled layer growth of 0.46 Å per cycle. The NbN thin films are deposited on undoped Si(100) using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD), with the metal–organic compound (tertbutylimido)-tris (diethylamino)-niobium (TBTDEN) and an hydrogen plasma as precursors. The ALD process enables the production of superconducting NbN layers with precise control over chemical composition, crystal structure, and film thickness, which are essential for realizing the CQUID.
